blocks.content: A PersistentVolumeClaim stuck Pending means it has not bound to a PV yet, either because no matching one exists (static provisioning) or dynamic provisioning itself never succeeded.
A PVC stuck in this state simply has not found, or been given, a matching PV, exactly the binding mechanism covered in the Persistent Volume Claim topic in the Storage module.

blocks.alt: The binding, covered in the Storage module, simply has not happened yet

blocks.content: 2. Static vs Dynamic, the Same Symptom
blocks.text: 2. Static vs Dynamic, the Same Symptom

blocks.content: Whether the cluster uses static provisioning (no administrator-created PV happens to match) or dynamic provisioning (the StorageClass's provisioner tried and genuinely failed), covered in their own topics, both present as the exact same Pending state.

blocks.alt: Two different underlying causes, presenting as the exact same visible symptom

blocks.content: 3. Common Cause: No StorageClass, No Default
blocks.text: 3. Common Cause: No StorageClass, No Default

blocks.content: If a PVC specifies no storageClassName, and the cluster has no default StorageClass configured either, exactly the default-class behavior covered in the StorageClass topic, there is nothing for dynamic provisioning to actually act on.

blocks.alt: Nothing for dynamic provisioning to act on, with no class specified or defaulted

blocks.content: 4. Common Cause: an Unsupported Access Mode
blocks.text: 4. Common Cause: an Unsupported Access Mode

blocks.content: Exactly the gotcha flagged in the Access Modes topic, requesting ReadWriteMany when the available storage backend only supports ReadWriteOnce means no PV can ever satisfy the claim, it stays Pending indefinitely.

blocks.alt: The exact access mode gotcha flagged directly in its own dedicated topic

blocks.content: kubectl describe pvc states the actual reason in its Events section, exactly the same pattern as every other describe-based diagnosis covered throughout this module, always the fastest path to the real answer.

blocks.alt: The same describe-and-check-Events pattern, applied here to storage specifically

blocks.content:
kubectl describe pvc my-app-storage
# Events:
#   Warning  ProvisioningFailed  no persistent volumes available for this claim

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A Pending PVC means no PV has bound to it, missing StorageClass configuration and unsupported access modes are the most common recurring causes.
kubectl describe pvc's Events section states the actual reason directly, exactly the same diagnostic pattern used throughout this entire module.
